You are acting as a Principal Engineer and Open Source Maintainer for this repository.

Your task is NOT to add new runtime features or optimize the code.

Instead, your goal is to significantly improve the project's engineering maturity, maintainability, contributor experience, and long-term architectural sustainability.

Assume this project aims to become one of the best open-source data movement / ETL / connector frameworks.

Think like the maintainers of:

- Kubernetes
- Rust
- Apache Arrow
- dbt
- Apache Airflow
- Dagster
- DuckDB
- Terraform
- Tokio

Your mission is to leave the repository in a significantly better state than before, without changing its external behavior.

----------------------------------------
OBJECTIVES
----------------------------------------

Improve the repository by adding missing engineering artifacts, architecture documentation, design documentation, contributor guidance, and long-term governance.

Do NOT make cosmetic documentation.

Everything should help future contributors understand WHY the system is designed the way it is.

Focus on maintainability over features.

----------------------------------------
TASK 1 — Create Architecture Documentation
----------------------------------------

Create a new directory:

docs/architecture/

Populate it with comprehensive documentation.

Suggested structure:

docs/
└── architecture/
    ├── README.md
    ├── overview.md
    ├── execution.md
    ├── pipeline.md
    ├── stream-pages.md
    ├── connector-sdk.md
    ├── state-management.md
    ├── retries.md
    ├── recovery.md
    ├── observability.md
    ├── resilience.md
    ├── batching.md
    ├── schema.md
    ├── quality.md
    ├── contracts.md
    ├── masking.md
    ├── performance.md
    ├── extensibility.md
    └── roadmap.md

Each document should explain:

• Why this subsystem exists
• What problem it solves
• Major components
• Execution flow
• Important invariants
• Trade-offs
• Failure scenarios
• Future evolution
• Related modules

Do not simply describe code.

Explain architecture.

----------------------------------------
TASK 2 — Architecture Decision Records
----------------------------------------

Create

docs/adr/

Write Architecture Decision Records for every major architectural decision.

Examples:

0001-stream-pages.md

0002-checkpoint-ordering.md

0003-builder-pattern.md

0004-json-record-model.md

0005-runtime-recovery.md

0006-state-management.md

0007-retries.md

0009-schema-validation.md

0010-pipeline-runtime.md

Each ADR should contain

- Status
- Context
- Problem
- Decision
- Alternatives Considered
- Trade-offs
- Consequences
- Future Work

Do not invent decisions.

Infer them from the implementation.

----------------------------------------
TASK 3 — Architecture Diagrams
----------------------------------------

Create Mermaid diagrams throughout the documentation.

Examples:

Pipeline execution

Connector lifecycle

Retry flow

Recovery flow

Checkpoint lifecycle

State management

Execution runtime

Quality pipeline

Masking pipeline

Contract validation

Observability flow

Every major subsystem should have a visual diagram.

----------------------------------------
TASK 4 — Contributor Guide
----------------------------------------

Create

docs/contributing/

Include

architecture.md

connector-authoring.md

testing.md

performance.md

debugging.md

common-mistakes.md

Explain

How to add connectors

How checkpoints work

How pagination works

How retries work

How state is managed

How testing should be written

What abstractions should be reused

What NOT to do

----------------------------------------
TASK 5 — Engineering Principles
----------------------------------------

Create

docs/engineering-principles.md

Describe principles such as

Composition over inheritance

Small focused traits

Progressive APIs

Observable by default

Explicit state

Deterministic retries

Backward compatibility

Safe defaults

Minimal allocations

Developer ergonomics

Explain WHY every principle exists.

----------------------------------------
TASK 6 — Repository Roadmap
----------------------------------------

Create

docs/roadmap.md

Divide work into

Near Term

Medium Term

Long Term

Examples

Documentation

Connector ecosystem

Plugin system

Capability traits

Arrow integration

Zero-copy execution

Performance

Certification

Benchmark suite

SDK improvements

Avoid promises.

Focus on architectural direction.

----------------------------------------
TASK 7 — Repository Standards
----------------------------------------

Create

docs/standards/

Include

api-design.md

error-handling.md

logging.md

testing.md

performance.md

state.md

Each document should define repository-wide conventions.

----------------------------------------
TASK 8 — Public API Stability
----------------------------------------

Create

docs/stability.md

Categorize APIs into

Stable

Experimental

Internal

Deprecated

Explain compatibility expectations.

----------------------------------------
TASK 9 — RFC Process
----------------------------------------

Create

rfcs/

Include templates for future RFCs.

Also include several example RFCs.

Examples

Capability Traits

Arrow Support

Plugin System

Streaming Improvements

Async Connector Runtime

Each RFC should explain motivation and trade-offs.

----------------------------------------
TASK 10 — Architecture Review
----------------------------------------

Create

docs/architecture-review.md

Write an objective review of the repository.

Include

Strengths

Weaknesses

Future Risks

Scalability

Technical Debt

Architectural Debt

Maintenance Risks

Contributor Experience

Testing

Documentation

Performance

Extensibility

Do not fabricate problems.

Support every observation with evidence from the implementation.

----------------------------------------
TASK 11 — Design Invariants
----------------------------------------

Document critical invariants.

Examples

Bookmarks are never persisted before durable writes.

Retries never advance state.

State reflects committed work.

StreamPage ordering.

Execution guarantees.

Cancellation semantics.

Recovery guarantees.

These invariants should become part of the official documentation.

----------------------------------------
TASK 12 — Review Existing Documentation
----------------------------------------

Review every existing markdown document.

Improve them where necessary.

Avoid duplication.

Cross-reference related documents.

Maintain consistent terminology.

----------------------------------------
TASK 13 — Cross Linking
----------------------------------------

Every documentation page should reference related pages.

For example

Execution

↓

State

↓

Recovery

↓

Retries

↓

Observability

The documentation should feel like a coherent book rather than isolated files.

----------------------------------------
TASK 14 — Documentation Quality
----------------------------------------

Documentation should read like official engineering documentation.

Not blog posts.

Not tutorials.

Not marketing.

Every statement should help future maintainers.

----------------------------------------
TASK 15 — Final Review
----------------------------------------

Before finishing

Perform a complete review.

Ensure

No duplicated concepts

Consistent terminology

Consistent diagrams

Consistent style

Correct cross references

No dead links

Good navigation

Logical progression

The documentation should feel like something maintained by a large engineering organization.

----------------------------------------
IMPORTANT
----------------------------------------

Do NOT rewrite the runtime.

Do NOT introduce breaking changes.

Do NOT redesign working abstractions.

Do NOT replace serde_json.

Do NOT split crates unnecessarily.

Do NOT optimize code without evidence.

The objective is engineering maturity, documentation quality, contributor experience, architectural clarity, and long-term maintainability.

If you identify implementation improvements while working, document them separately rather than changing behavior automatically.

The final result should make this repository feel like a flagship open-source project with world-class documentation and architecture guidance.

# Contributing to faucet-stream

Thanks for your interest in contributing! faucet-stream is a Rust workspace of
connector crates plus the `faucet` CLI, and it's designed as an ecosystem — both
core changes and third-party connectors are welcome.

By participating you agree to abide by our [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Getting set up

```bash
git clone https://github.com/PawanSikawat/faucet-stream
cd faucet-stream
cargo build --workspace
```

The toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`. Some connectors link native
libraries — the **Kafka** connectors build `librdkafka`, which needs `cmake` and
a C toolchain (`libsasl2-dev libssl-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev` on Debian/Ubuntu).

## Before you open a PR

Run the same checks CI runs:

```bash
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features        # Kafka integration tests need Docker
cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps   # must be warning-free
```

For pipelines that touch real services, the [`examples/`](./examples/) directory
has a `docker compose` stack and `make demo` for a no-infrastructure smoke test.

## Tests

- New functions and behaviors **must** have tests — untested public API is a
  liability. Unit tests live in `#[cfg(test)]` modules; HTTP-based connectors use
  `wiremock` integration tests under the crate's `tests/`.

# Architecture

*The maintainer's guide to how faucet-stream works and why it is built this way.*

This tree documents the *architecture* of faucet-stream — the reasoning,
invariants, and trade-offs behind the implementation. It is written for
maintainers and contributors, not end users; the user-facing how-to lives in
the [mdBook](../book/src/introduction.md).

Every page here is grounded in the implementation and cites the modules it
describes. When code and these docs disagree, the code is right and the doc is
a bug — fix it.

## How to read this

Read top-to-bottom the first time; the pages build on each other. The spine
below is the data path a single record travels, in order.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "CLI orchestration (cli/)"
      cfg["config + expand"] --> exec["executor"]
    end
    exec --> pipe["Pipeline"]
    pipe --> rs["run_stream loop"]
    subgraph "faucet-core"
      rs --> src["Source::stream_pages"]
      rs --> passes["masking → quality → contract → drift"]
      rs --> sink["Sink::write_batch*"]
      rs --> state["StateStore checkpoint"]
    end
    state -. resume .-> src
```

### The execution spine (read in order)

1. [Overview](./overview.md) — the whole system in one page: crates, layers, and the shape of a run.
2. [Execution model](./execution.md) — how a config becomes running pipelines (CLI expand → executor → core), and what the core deliberately does *not* own.
3. [Pipeline](./pipeline.md) — `Pipeline` and `run_stream`: the orchestration loop and its per-page phases.
4. [Stream pages](./stream-pages.md) — the `StreamPage` streaming contract and bounded-memory model.
5. [State management](./state-management.md) — `StateStore`, bookmarks, and state keys.
6. [Recovery](./recovery.md) — what happens after a crash; sink-anchored resume.
7. [Retries](./retries.md) — the two retry layers and the never-duplicate rule.
8. [Resilience](./resilience.md) — the unified retry / circuit-breaker / poison-pill policy.
9. [Observability](./observability.md) — automatic instrumentation, metrics, and cardinality discipline.

### The data-shaping subsystems

- [Batching](./batching.md) — page sizing, the `batch_size = 0` sentinel, adaptive batching.
- [Schema](./schema.md) — inference and the layered per-page validation passes.
- [Quality](./quality.md) — per-record / per-batch data-quality checks.
- [Contracts](./contracts.md) — versioned output-schema promises.
- [Masking](./masking.md) — PII detection and column masking (runs first).

### Cross-cutting

- [Connector SDK](./connector-sdk.md) — the `Source` / `Sink` traits and connector conventions.
- [Performance](./performance.md) — the throughput/efficiency disciplines.
- [Extensibility](./extensibility.md) — the marketplace / plugin model.
- [Design invariants](./invariants.md) — the load-bearing rules; **read this if you touch the write path.**
- [Roadmap](./roadmap.md) — architectural direction.

## The one invariant to remember

> **A page's bookmark is persisted to the state store only *after* the sink has
> durably written and flushed that page.**

Everything about correctness under failure follows from this. It is enforced in
`run_stream` (`crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`) across all three write paths and is
documented in [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-checkpoint-ordering.md) and
[invariants](./invariants.md).

## Related

- [Documentation home](../README.md)
- [Architecture Decision Records](../adr/)
- [Engineering principles](../engineering-principles.md)
- [Architecture review](../architecture-review.md)

# Execution model *How a declarative config becomes running pipelines — and the deliberate line between the CLI runtime and the core library.* ## Why this exists faucet-stream has two very different execution audiences: 1. **Config-driven operators** who write a YAML/JSON file and run `faucet run`. They need matrix fan-out, templating, scheduling, an HTTP control plane, and clustering. 2. **Rust embedders** who construct a `Pipeline` in code and call `.run()`. They need none of the above — just the moving-data engine. The architecture serves both by drawing a hard line: **`faucet-core` is the engine; all orchestration is CLI-layer code built on top of it.** The core never learns about cron, HTTP, DAGs, or clusters. This keeps the crate that 60+ connectors depend on small, stable, and embeddable, and confines the churn of new runtime features to `cli/`. See [ADR 0010 — Pipeline runtime](../adr/0010-pipeline-runtime.md) for the decision and its alternatives. ## The stages of a run ```mermaid flowchart TD A["config file (YAML/JSON)"] --> B["compose
extends / !include / profiles"] B --> C["interpolate
env / file / secret / vars / template refs"] C --> D["secrets pass
vault / aws-sm / gcp-sm / azure-kv"] D --> E["PipelineConfig (parsed, deny_unknown_fields)"] E --> F["expand → Vec<ExpandedNode>
matrix fan-out, template selection, gates"] F --> G["executor::run_expanded
bounded Semaphore, JoinSet, on_error policy"] G --> H["per node: build_source / build_sink / state"] H --> I["faucet_core::Pipeline::run"] I --> J["run_stream loop"] ``` Each stage is a pure, separately testable transform of the one before it. The boundary between "still a config document" and "a running pipeline" is `expand`. ### 1. Compose (`cli/src/compose.rs`) A front pre-pass that stitches `extends:` inheritance, substitutes `!include` fragments, and overlays the selected `profiles:` block, then strips the metadata keys before the strict (`deny_unknown_fields`) `PipelineConfig` parser sees them. File-loads only — a config submitted to `faucet serve` over HTTP never touches the filesystem, so compose is skipped there. ### 2. Interpolate (`cli/src/interpolate.rs`) Three staged substitutions: load-time `${env:…}` / `${file:…}` / `${secret:…}`; post-parse `${vars.X}` and `${sources/sinks.NAME.PATH}` template references; and deferred `${row_id.path}` / `${now.*}` tokens resolved per-invocation at runtime. Cycles surface as typed errors, never as silent empty strings. ### 3. Secrets (`cli/src/secrets/`) The final load-time stage: `${vault:…}` / `${aws-sm:…}` / `${gcp-sm:…}` / `${azure-kv:…}` are resolved concurrently and substituted into the parsed tree. A redaction boundary scrubs resolved values from faucet's own log output — but only faucet's own output (see [logging standard](../standards/logging.md)). ### 4. Expand (`cli/src/expand.rs`) Turns one `PipelineConfig` into a `Vec` — one node per matrix invocation. It: - selects source/sink templates (`ref` → named template, else `default`); - deep-merges per-row `kind`/`config` overrides (`cli/src/merge.rs`: scalars replace, objects merge, arrays replace wholesale); - validates ids, parent/child edges, `depends_on` edges (Kahn's algorithm over the combined graph), and template names; - **enforces the load-time gates** — the exactly-once dual gate, the `write_mode × sink` gate, the `schema: evolve` gate, and the quarantine-requires-DLQ gates — so an impossible config is rejected *before any run starts*, not mid-stream. Emitting nodes in BFS order (roots before children) is what lets the executor start roots immediately. ### 5. Executor (`cli/src/executor.rs`) `run_expanded(nodes, ExecuteOptions)` drives the nodes under one bounded `Semaphore` shared across roots and per-parent-record child fan-outs. Both `on_error` modes run in parallel via `JoinSet`: - `continue` — a failed subtree is skipped; siblings finish. - `stop` — the level's `CancellationToken` is cancelled on first failure so in-flight pipelines **flush at their next page boundary** (a buffered Parquet footer / S3 multipart survives), then any that don't stop within `STOP_FLUSH_GRACE` are hard-aborted. Each invocation's source is wrapped with a `StateKeyOverride` so per-row state keys override the source's natural one (see [state](./state-management.md)). ### 6. Core (`crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`) The executor builds the source/sink/state and calls `faucet_core::Pipeline::run`, which drives the `run_stream` loop. From here on, nothing knows it was launched from a config — an embedder reaches the exact same code by constructing a `Pipeline` directly. See [pipeline](./pipeline.md). ## Orchestration runtimes are all "expand + executor + a loop" `schedule`, `serve`, `replicate`, and `backfill` are **not** new engines. Each is a thin CLI-layer loop around the same `expand` + `executor` path: | Runtime | What it adds around expand+executor | |---------|-------------------------------------| | `run` | one pass, then exit | | `schedule` | a cron tick loop (`croner` + `chrono-tz`), overlap policy, run timeout | | `serve` | an axum HTTP control plane, a bounded queue, run history, RBAC, clustering | | `replicate` | a two-phase snapshot→CDC handoff anchored by `capture_resume_position` | | `backfill` | a windowed replay over a bounded `--from/--to` range | Because they share the engine, they inherit every gate and every durability guarantee for free. The only `faucet-core` change any of them required was one new *defaulted* trait method (`capture_resume_position` for `replicate`) — the strongest possible evidence the core/CLI split is holding. ## Invariants - **The core owns no scheduling.** Any timer, HTTP endpoint, or DAG lives in `cli/`. A change to how runs are triggered must not touch `faucet-core`. - **Gates run at load time, in `expand`.** An invalid topology (bad exactly-once combo, unsupported write mode, quarantine without DLQ) fails `faucet validate` before a single record moves. - **Config transforms are pure.** compose → interpolate → secrets → parse → expand are each testable in isolation and free of I/O beyond their named side-effect (file reads for compose/interpolate, network for secrets). ## Failure scenarios - **Malformed config** → typed `CliError::Config` at parse/expand, before any run. No partial execution. - **A root fails under `on_error: stop`** → the level cancels cooperatively; in-flight sinks flush; the run reports the failure without corrupting output. - **A child's parent fails** → the child (and its subtree/dependents) is skipped, mirroring the failed-dependency cascade. ## Future evolution Richer runtime features (more trigger types, cluster scheduling policies) keep landing in `cli/`. The test that the split is healthy: a new runtime feature should need *zero or one defaulted* `faucet-core` change. See [architecture roadmap](./roadmap.md). ## Related - [Overview](./overview.md) · [Pipeline engine](./pipeline.md) - [State management](./state-management.md) · [Recovery](./recovery.md) - [ADR 0010 — Pipeline runtime](../adr/0010-pipeline-runtime.md) - Full CLI/runtime internals: [`.claude/rules/architecture.md`](../../.claude/rules/architecture.md) - User guide: [Core concepts](../book/src/getting-started/concepts.md)

result.output:
1	# Pipeline engine
2	
3	*The `Pipeline` / `run_stream` core: one page-at-a-time loop that owns the write→flush→checkpoint contract.*
4	
5	## Why it exists
6	
7	`Pipeline` is the single place where a source, a sink, a state store, and the
8	protection/validation passes are wired together and driven. Concentrating this in
9	one function (`run_stream`, `crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`) means the
10	data-integrity ordering is written **once** and every connector inherits it — no
11	connector can get checkpointing wrong because no connector implements it.
12	
13	## Major components
14	
15	- **`Pipeline<'a, So, Si>`** — a builder over borrowed `&Source` / `&Sink`
16	  (object-safe, so `Box<dyn Source>` works). Configured progressively with
17	  `with_state_store`, `with_dlq`, `with_quality`, `with_contract`, `with_masking`,
18	  `with_schema_drift`, `with_resilience`, `with_delivery`, `with_cancel`,
19	  `with_adaptive`. See [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-builder-pattern.md).
20	- **`Pipeline::run`** — resolves run identity (name/row/run_id), wraps the source,
21	  sink, and state store in observability decorators, performs bookmark resume, then
22	  hands off to `run_stream`.
23	- **`run_stream`** — the free function that drives the page loop. Also callable
24	  directly by library authors who already have a `Stream<StreamPage>`.
25	- **`RunStreamOptions`** — the option bag carrying everything the loop needs
26	  (state, dlq, quality, contract, masking, drift, resilience, delivery, cancel).
27	- **`StreamPage { records, bookmark }`** / **`PipelineResult`** — the unit of work
28	  and the run summary. See [stream-pages](./stream-pages.md).
29	
30	## Execution flow
31	
32	```mermaid
33	flowchart TD
34	    START[Pipeline::run] --> RESUME[resume: read bookmark, apply_start_bookmark]
35	    RESUME --> SINKANCHOR[exactly-once: re-anchor from sink watermark]
36	    SINKANCHOR --> LOOP{next page?}
37	    LOOP -->|cancelled| FLUSHOUT[flush + return partial]
38	    LOOP -->|Some page| MASK[mask → quality → contract → drift]
39	    MASK --> PATH{write path}
40	    PATH -->|DLQ| WDLQ[write_batch_partial + route failures]
41	    PATH -->|exactly-once| WEO[write_batch_idempotent skip-if-committed]
42	    PATH -->|default| WDEF[write_batch]
43	    WDLQ & WEO & WDEF --> BM{page has bookmark?}
44	    BM -->|yes| FLUSH[flush → checkpoint]
45	    BM -->|no| LOOP
46	    FLUSH --> LOOP
47	    LOOP -->|None| DONE[flush + PipelineResult]
48	```
49	
50	### The three write paths
51	
52	`run_stream` branches on configuration into three mutually exclusive paths, each
53	of which preserves the checkpoint-ordering invariant:
54	
55	1. **DLQ path** — `write_batch_partial` splits per-row successes from failures;
56	   failures are enveloped and routed to the DLQ sink; then flush + checkpoint. A
57	   deferred abort (DLQ budget, circuit breaker, drift-`fail`) fires *after* the page
58	   is durable so nothing is stranded.
59	2. **Exactly-once path** — issues a monotonic commit token per bookmark-carrying
60	   page (`format_token_with_bookmark`), skips the write if the sink's committed seq
61	   is already ≥ the page's (idempotent replay), else `write_batch_idempotent`; then
62	   flush + `wrap_state(bookmark, seq)` checkpoint. See [recovery](./recovery.md).
63	3. **Default path** — `write_batch`, then (on a bookmark-carrying page) flush +
64	   checkpoint. This is the at-least-once baseline.
65	
66	## Invariants
67	
68	- **Write → flush → checkpoint, always.** In all three paths the bookmark is
69	  persisted only after `write_batch*` and `flush()` both return `Ok`. This is *the*
70	  data-integrity invariant — see [invariants](./invariants.md) and
71	  [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-checkpoint-ordering.md).
72	- **Empty, bookmark-less pages are skipped** (`records.is_empty() && bookmark.is_none()`).
73	- **A bookmark-less page is written but not checkpointed** — it stays at-least-once
74	  for that page (rare; CDC sources bookmark every committed transaction).
75	- **Every early exit flushes.** The loop runs inside an inner future; a source
76	  error, a propagated write/flush/state error, or a cancellation all fall through to
77	  a best-effort final flush, so a buffered sink (Parquet footer, S3 multipart)
78	  commits what it has rather than orphaning the file.
79	- **Masking runs first, unconditionally**, before any sink, the DLQ, or a lineage
80	  sample observes the records. See [masking](./masking.md).
81	
82	## Trade-offs
83	
84	- **One page in memory at a time** bounds memory at `O(batch_size)` but ties
85	  throughput to page size and sink round-trip latency (mitigated by
86	  [adaptive batching](./batching.md) and sink-side bulk APIs).
87	- **Fixed pass order** removes a config knob but eliminates PII-leak and
88	  bad-row-written bug classes. See [schema](./schema.md).
89	- **A single hot loop** keeps the contract in one place but means new cross-cutting
90	  behaviour (a new pass) is a change to `run_stream` itself — reviewed with care.
91	
92	## Failure scenarios
93	
94	- **Crash between flush and checkpoint** → at-least-once replays the page;
95	  exactly-once skips it via the committed token. No data loss either way; only
96	  at-least-once risks duplicates. See [recovery](./recovery.md).
97	- **Sink commits server-side but the response is lost, then a retry fires** →
98	  duplication, unless the sink is idempotent. The retry layer refuses to retry a
99	  non-idempotent `write_batch` for exactly this reason — see [retries](./retries.md).
100	- **A validation pass aborts** → `contract: fail` writes nothing from the page;
101	  `drift: fail` defers until survivors are durable.
102	
103	## Future evolution
104	
105	- Batch-level parallelism across sinks without breaking per-page ordering.
106	- A columnar page type behind the same loop ([RFC 0002](../../rfcs/0002-arrow-support.md)).

# Stream pages *The `StreamPage` streaming contract — the unit of work that bounds memory and carries checkpoints.* ## Why this exists A data-movement tool must move datasets larger than memory. The naive design — fetch everything from the source, then write everything to the sink — buffers `O(total)` records on both sides and falls over on a 100M-row table. The `StreamPage` model exists to make **bounded memory the default**, without asking every connector to reinvent chunking or checkpointing. It also solves a second problem: *where does a checkpoint belong?* By attaching an optional bookmark to each page, the source declares exactly which points in the stream are safe to resume from, and the pipeline gets a uniform place to persist them. See [ADR 0001](../adr/0001-stream-pages.md). ## The contract ```rust pub struct StreamPage { pub records: Vec, // this page's chunk of records pub bookmark: Option, // Some ⇒ safe to checkpoint after this page is durable } ``` A source implements: ```rust fn stream_pages<'a>(&'a self, ctx: &'a Context, batch_size: usize) -> Pin> + Send + 'a>>; ``` (`crates/core/src/traits.rs`). The pipeline consumes the stream one page at a time in `run_stream` (`crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`), writing each page to the sink as it arrives. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Source P1["StreamPage #1
records, bookmark=None"] P2["StreamPage #2
records, bookmark=None"] P3["StreamPage #3
records, bookmark=Some"] end P1 --> W1[write + hold] --> P2 P2 --> W2[write + hold] --> P3 P3 --> W3[write] --> F[flush] --> C[checkpoint bookmark] ``` ## Bookmark semantics — who emits `Some`, and when The `bookmark` field is the entire checkpointing protocol: - **Query/snapshot sources** (a REST endpoint, a `SELECT`) usually know their resume value only after seeing every record — the max value of an incrementing column. They emit `bookmark: None` on every page except the last, and `Some(max_value)` on the final page. - **CDC / log sources** (postgres-cdc, mysql-cdc, mongodb-cdc, kafka) know a safe resume position at every committed transaction / offset boundary. They emit `Some(position)` **per committed transaction**, so they get per-transaction durability automatically — no special-casing in the pipeline. The pipeline treats both identically: *whenever a page carries `Some(bookmark)`, flush the sink and persist the bookmark before polling the next page.* This is the write→flush→checkpoint invariant (see [invariants](./invariants.md)). ## The default implementation `Source::stream_pages` has a default that chunks `fetch_all()` into `batch_size`-sized pages, emitting the bookmark on the last page. This means a connector author gets bounded-memory streaming **for free** — they only override `stream_pages` when the underlying protocol has a native streaming primitive worth exploiting (a server cursor, the Kafka consumer, an Arrow async reader). Sources that override it to stream natively: `rest`, `graphql`, `postgres`, `postgres-cdc`, `mysql`, `mysql-cdc`, `mssql`, `sqlite`, `mongodb`, `mongodb-cdc`, `s3` (JSONL/RawText), `gcs` (JSONL/RawText), `parquet`, `csv`, `xml`, `elasticsearch` (scroll), `kafka`, `kinesis`, `spanner`, `websocket`, `redis`, `grpc` (server-streaming). Sources that intentionally keep the default: `grpc` unary (no paging primitive) and `webhook` (buffer-shaped by nature). ## The `batch_size` hint vs the config knob `batch_size` is passed *into* `stream_pages`, but on every overriding source it is **informational** — the source uses its own config field as the authoritative knob. This prevents a pipeline-supplied hint from silently overriding an explicit per-connector setting. `batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel (one page for the whole dataset); the caps live in `validate_batch_size`. See [batching](./batching.md). ## Invariants - **One page of records is held at a time** on each side — memory is `O(batch_size)`, independent of dataset size. - **A bookmark marks a durable-resume point**, nothing more. A page with `bookmark: None` is written but never checkpointed. - **An empty, bookmark-less page is a no-op** and is skipped by the loop. - **Page order is preserved** — pages are consumed strictly in stream order, and checkpoints advance monotonically. ## Trade-offs - **Throughput is coupled to page size and sink latency.** A tiny `batch_size` means many round-trips; a huge one raises memory and the blast radius of a failed page. [Adaptive batching](./batching.md) tunes this at runtime. - **The bookmark is an opaque `Value`.** The pipeline never interprets it, which keeps the contract simple and connector-agnostic, but means correctness of the resume logic lives entirely inside the source (`apply_start_bookmark`). - **No cross-page pipelining today.** The current loop reads page N+1 only after page N is durable. Overlapping read and write is a candidate future change — see [RFC 0004](../../rfcs/0004-streaming-improvements.md) — and must preserve the checkpoint-ordering invariant. ## Failure scenarios - **Source errors mid-stream** → the `Err` item propagates; the loop flushes best-effort and returns the error. Pages already checkpointed stay durable. - **An empty page arrives mid-stream** (e.g. a REST page with zero records) → handled by the source's termination logic; a bookmark-less empty page is skipped, so it cannot advance the checkpoint past unwritten data. - **A malformed bookmark** → surfaced when the source's `apply_start_bookmark` rejects it on the next run, not silently ignored. ## Future evolution - Read/write pipelining and explicit backpressure ([RFC 0004](../../rfcs/0004-streaming-improvements.md)). - A columnar `StreamPage` variant behind a feature flag ([RFC 0002](../../rfcs/0002-arrow-support.md)). ## Related - [Pipeline engine](./pipeline.md) · [Batching](./batching.md) - [State management](./state-management.md) · [Recovery](./recovery.md) - [Connector SDK](./connector-sdk.md) - [ADR 0001 — Stream pages](../adr/0001-stream-pages.md) - Connector streaming rules: [`.claude/rules/connectors.md`](../../.claude/rules/connectors.md)

2	
3	*Durable bookmarks, the `StateStore` abstraction, and the key scheme that makes every invocation independently resumable.*
4	
5	## Why it exists
6	
7	Incremental replication and crash recovery both need one thing: a durable record of
8	"how far did we get". faucet-stream calls that record a **bookmark** and stores it
9	through a single narrow abstraction, the `StateStore`. Keeping state behind one
10	trait means connectors never talk to a state backend directly — they produce and
11	consume opaque bookmark values, and the pipeline handles persistence with the
12	correct ordering. See [ADR 0006](../adr/0006-state-management.md).
13	
14	## Major components
15	
16	- **`StateStore`** (`crates/core/src/state.rs`) — an async trait with three
17	  operations over `serde_json::Value`:
18	
19	  ```rust
20	  async fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<Value>, FaucetError>;
21	  async fn put(&self, key: &str, value: &Value) -> Result<(), FaucetError>;
22	  async fn delete(&self, key: &str) -> Result<(), FaucetError>;
23	  ```
24	
25	- **Built-in backends in core** — `MemoryStateStore` (ephemeral, single-process) and
26	  `FileStateStore` (one JSON file per key, written via atomic rename, optional
27	  at-rest encryption). Kept in `faucet-core` because they add no dependencies.
28	- **Heavier backends in their own crates** — `faucet-state-redis`
29	  (`{namespace}:{key}`) and `faucet-state-postgres` (a single
30	  `faucet_state(key, value, updated_at)` table with `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`). These
31	  live outside core so `faucet-core` stays dependency-light. See
32	  [ADR 0006](../adr/0006-state-management.md) and [ADR 0010](../adr/0010-pipeline-runtime.md).
33	- **`validate_state_key`** — rejects empty, hidden (`.`-prefixed), and traversal-
34	  unsafe keys, so a key can be used as a filename component without escaping the
35	  store's root.
36	
37	## How a bookmark flows
38	
39	```mermaid
40	sequenceDiagram
41	    participant SS as StateStore
42	    participant P as Pipeline
43	    participant Src as Source
44	    participant Snk as Sink
45	    P->>SS: get(state_key)
46	    SS-->>P: prior bookmark (or None)
47	    P->>Src: apply_start_bookmark(prior)
48	    loop each page
49	        Src-->>P: StreamPage{records, bookmark}
50	        P->>Snk: write_batch(records)
51	        P->>Snk: flush()
52	        P->>SS: put(state_key, bookmark)
53	    end
54	```
55	
56	The `put` happens **after** `write_batch` + `flush` — never before. That ordering
57	is the whole point; it is documented as the central invariant in
58	[invariants](./invariants.md) and [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-checkpoint-ordering.md).
59	
60	## The state-key scheme
61	
62	A key identifies a resumable position uniquely across the matrix DAG:
63	
64	| Node | Key |
65	|---|---|
66	| Source's natural key | `Source::state_key()` (e.g. `postgres-cdc:<slot>`) |
67	| Matrix root row | `{name}::{row_id}` |
68	| Matrix child (per parent record) | `{name}::{row_id}::{parent_record_key}` |
69	| Replication CDC node | `{name}::cdc`; phase marker `{name}::__replication__` |
70	| Backfill unit | `{name}::backfill::{unit}` (live bookmark untouched) |
71	
72	The executor wraps each invocation's source with a `StateKeyOverride` so the
73	per-row key wins over the source's natural key. This is why two matrix rows using
74	the same connector never clobber each other's progress.
75	
76	## Exactly-once: the state envelope
77	
78	Under `delivery: exactly_once` (atomic-watermark mechanism) the stored value is not
79	a bare bookmark but an envelope carrying both the bookmark and the monotonic
80	sequence: `wrap_state(bookmark, seq)` / `unwrap_state(value)`
81	(`crates/core/src/idempotency.rs`). The sequence lets recovery reconcile the state
82	store against the sink's committed watermark. See [recovery](./recovery.md).
83	
84	## Invariants
85	
86	- **A bookmark is persisted only after a durable, flushed write.** (The central
87	  invariant.)
88	- **Keys are validated before use** on every `get`/`put`/`delete`, so a malformed
89	  key fails loudly rather than escaping the store root.
90	- **The bookmark is opaque to the store.** The store round-trips a `Value`; only the
91	  source interprets it. This keeps the store fully generic.
92	- **`memory` state is not durable.** Gates that require durability
93	  (`delivery: exactly_once`, SLA baselines) reject or warn on the memory backend at
94	  config-load.
95	
96	## Trade-offs
97	
98	- **`Value`-typed, three-method interface** maximises backend portability at the
99	  cost of any store-specific optimisation (range scans, TTLs). Bookmarks are tiny
100	  and low-frequency, so this is the right trade.
101	- **One file per key** (FileStateStore) is simple and atomic but not ideal for
102	  thousands of matrix children — that is what the Redis/Postgres backends are for.
103	
104	## Failure scenarios

106	- **Store unreachable at checkpoint** → the `put` errors, the run aborts after a
107	  flush; the next run re-reads the last durable bookmark and replays from there
108	  (at-least-once) or skips (exactly-once).
109	- **Corrupt/legacy stored value** → `unwrap_state` tolerates a bare bookmark
110	  (legacy) vs. an envelope, so upgrading delivery modes does not strand state.
111

115	  concurrent writers to one key.
116	- A typed bookmark trait so sources can express bookmark *comparability* (for

# Recovery

*What happens after a crash — how a run resumes without losing or duplicating data, including sink-anchored exactly-once resume.*

## Why this exists

Any long-running data movement will be interrupted: a process is killed, a
network partitions, a node is rescheduled. Recovery is the set of guarantees
about what the *next* run does with the work the crashed run left behind. The
design goal is blunt: **never lose data, and under exactly-once never duplicate
it** — the two worst outcomes for a data pipeline.

Recovery is not a separate subsystem; it is an emergent property of the
[checkpoint-ordering invariant](./invariants.md) plus a small amount of
resume logic in `Pipeline::run` (`crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`).

## The crash window

Every page passes through the same ordered steps:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    W["write_batch*"] --> F["flush()"] --> C["StateStore::put(bookmark)"]
    F -.->|CRASH HERE| X((crash))
```

The only interesting crash point is **between `flush()` and `put`**: the sink
has durably committed page N, but the state store still points at page N−1. On
restart, the source is re-anchored to N−1 and *replays page N*. What the replay
does depends on the delivery mode.

## At-least-once recovery (default)

The next run reads the last durable bookmark, calls
`Source::apply_start_bookmark`, and re-fetches from there. Any page whose write
committed but whose bookmark did not persist is written **again**. This is safe
for data loss (nothing is skipped) but may duplicate rows. That is the explicit
contract of at-least-once, and it is why append-only sinks and downstream
idempotency matter. See [retries](./retries.md) for the closely-related
"lost response" duplication risk.

## Exactly-once recovery: two mechanisms

`delivery: exactly_once` upgrades the guarantee to *effectively-once* via one of
two mechanisms, selected in `run_stream` (`crates/core/src/idempotency.rs`):

### 1. Atomic-watermark

The sink commits the page's records **and** a monotonic commit token in one
atomic unit (a SQL transaction, an Iceberg snapshot property, a Kafka
transaction, a BigQuery multi-statement `MERGE`). On resume the pipeline reads
the sink's `last_committed_token(scope)`; if its sequence is ≥ the page's, the
page is **skipped** (`faucet_pipeline_pages_skipped_total` increments) instead
of rewritten.

Requirements (enforced as a hard gate at config-load in `cli/src/expand.rs`):
an idempotent sink, a deterministic-replay source, a durable (non-`memory`)
state store, and **no DLQ** (the DLQ and the atomic-watermark path are
incompatible in this version).

### 2. Keyed-upsert

If the sink is configured with `write_mode: upsert|delete` + a `key`, idempotence
comes from the sink's own keyed writes — replaying a page re-upserts the same
keys to the same values, a no-op. This works with **any** source, needs no
watermark, and allows a DLQ. The gate accepts this as the alternative to the
atomic-watermark requirements.

## Sink-anchored resume — closing the window cleanly (#291)

The subtle problem with the atomic-watermark mechanism: skipping a replayed page
by *counting sequence numbers* only works if the source replays the **exact same
page boundaries**. Log-positional sources like Kafka cannot promise that — the
next run's pages may be sliced differently.

The fix (verified in `Pipeline::run`, `crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`): the commit
token **embeds the page's resume bookmark**
(`format_token_with_bookmark(seq, bookmark)`). On resume, when the sink's
committed sequence is ahead of the state store, the pipeline reads that embedded
bookmark and calls `apply_start_bookmark` to re-anchor the source to the *exact
committed position* — then continues. Nothing is rewritten, and nothing depends
on identical replayed page boundaries. This is what qualifies the Kafka source
for exactly-once.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Pipeline::run
    participant SS as StateStore
    participant Snk as Sink
    participant Src as Source
    P->>SS: unwrap_state → (bookmark, start_seq)
    P->>Snk: last_committed_token(scope)
    Snk-->>P: token = format_token_with_bookmark(sink_seq, bm)
    alt sink_seq > start_seq (crash between flush and put)
        P->>Src: apply_start_bookmark(bm from token)
        Note over P: re-anchor to exact committed position; skip nothing
    else state store already current
        P->>Src: apply_start_bookmark(bookmark from state)
    end
```

Legacy bare tokens (written before bookmarks were embedded) parse with no
bookmark and fall back to the count-based skip path — the system stays
backward-compatible.

## Orchestration-level recovery (serve cluster)

Above the core, `faucet serve` adds recovery for *runs* (not pages). Each serve
process has a fresh `instance_id`; the SQL run table carries `owner` +
`lease_expires_at`. A lease loop heartbeats this instance's own non-terminal
runs and reclaims only runs whose owner's lease has **expired** — so a starting
or running instance never fails a live peer's in-flight runs on a shared
database (instance-fenced orphan recovery, #146 H7). This is CLI-layer logic; it
sits on top of, and does not change, the core recovery guarantees.

## Invariants

- **No data loss in any mode** — a crash re-fetches from the last durable
  bookmark; the write-before-checkpoint ordering guarantees the sink is never
  ahead of what will be re-read (or is reconciled via the watermark).
- **No duplication under exactly-once** — committed pages are skipped or
  re-anchored, never rewritten.
- **At-least-once may duplicate** — this is the documented, accepted contract.
- **Recovery is idempotent** — running the same crashed config again is always
  safe.

## Failure scenarios

- **Crash before `flush`** → page N is not durable; re-fetched and rewritten
  (both modes). Correct.
- **Crash between `flush` and `put`** → page N durable, state stale;
  at-least-once rewrites, exactly-once skips/re-anchors. Correct.
- **State store lost entirely** → the run restarts from the source's initial
  position; at-least-once re-emits everything (safe), exactly-once relies on the
  sink watermark to skip already-committed pages.
- **Serve node dies mid-run** → the lease expires; another instance reclaims and
  re-runs from the durable bookmark.

## Future evolution

- Extend sink-anchored resume to more log-positional sources as they gain
  exactly-once support.
- Compare-and-swap state writes to fence two writers to one key ([state](./state-management.md)).

## Related

- [Design invariants](./invariants.md) · [State management](./state-management.md)
- [Pipeline engine](./pipeline.md) · [Retries](./retries.md)
- [ADR 0002 — Checkpoint ordering](../adr/0002-checkpoint-ordering.md) · [ADR 0005 — Runtime recovery](../adr/0005-runtime-recovery.md)
- Exactly-once rules: [`.claude/rules/connectors.md`](../../.claude/rules/connectors.md)
- User guide: [Incremental replication & state](../book/src/cookbook/state.md)

# Design invariants

*The load-bearing guarantees the whole system depends on. If you change the write path, you are changing this file — update it deliberately.*

An invariant here is a rule the codebase relies on being true *everywhere*,
always. They are not aspirations; each is enforced in code and cited below.
Violating one silently corrupts data or breaks recovery — the worst class of
bug this project can ship. Treat this page as a contract with future
maintainers.

Every invariant lists **what it guarantees**, **where it is enforced**, and
**what breaks if you violate it**.

---

## I1 — A bookmark is persisted only after a durable, flushed write

**Guarantee.** For any page, the state store is updated with that page's
bookmark only *after* both `write_batch*` and `flush()` have returned `Ok`. The
ordering is always: **write → flush → checkpoint**. The state store is never
ahead of the sink.

**Where.** `run_stream` in `crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`, in all three write
paths (DLQ, exactly-once, default). Each ends with
`… sink.flush()? … store.put(key, bookmark)?`.

**If violated.** A crash after the checkpoint but before the write would skip
records permanently — silent data loss. This is the single most important rule
in the codebase. See [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-checkpoint-ordering.md),
[recovery](./recovery.md), [state](./state-management.md).

## I2 — Retries never advance state, and never retry a non-idempotent write

**Guarantee.** A retry re-attempts the *same* operation against the *same*
position; it never moves the bookmark forward. And a plain, non-idempotent
`write_batch` is retried **only** when the sink commits writes idempotently
(`Sink::supports_idempotent_writes()`); otherwise a lost-response retry could
duplicate every row.

**Where.** The `with_retry_write!` macro in `run_stream` gates retrying
non-idempotent writes on `sink.supports_idempotent_writes()`; the idempotent
path (`write_batch_idempotent`) is always safe to retry because replaying a
token-stamped write is a no-op.

**If violated.** Duplicated rows on a lost sink response — the repo's
#1-worst-bug class. See [retries](./retries.md), [ADR 0007](../adr/0007-retries.md).

## I3 — State reflects only committed work

**Guarantee.** A bookmark read on the next run points at a position for which
every prior record is durably in the sink. Under exactly-once the stored
`(bookmark, seq)` envelope is reconciled against the sink's committed watermark,
so the stored state is never treated as further ahead than the sink.

**Where.** `wrap_state`/`unwrap_state` + the sink-anchored resume block in
`Pipeline::run` (`crates/core/src/idempotency.rs`, `pipeline.rs`).

**If violated.** Recovery would resume past uncommitted data (loss) or
re-process committed data as if new (duplication under exactly-once).

## I4 — `StreamPage` ordering is preserved and checkpoints advance monotonically

**Guarantee.** Pages are consumed strictly in the order the source emits them;
checkpoints only ever move forward. Page N is fully durable before page N+1's
bookmark can be persisted.

**Where.** The single-threaded page loop in `run_stream`; there is no
concurrent consumption of the page stream.

**If violated.** Out-of-order checkpointing could persist a later bookmark while
an earlier page's write is still pending — reintroducing the I1 loss window.
See [stream-pages](./stream-pages.md).

## I5 — Masking runs first, before anything observes the records

**Guarantee.** When a masking policy is attached, the masking pass runs on each
page **before** the quality, contract, and drift passes, before any sink write,
before the DLQ, and before any lineage sample. No downstream component ever sees
unmasked PII.

**Where.** `run_stream` applies masking as the first per-page transformation
(`crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`, guarded by `#[cfg(feature = "masking")]`).

**If violated.** PII would leak to a sink, a DLQ envelope, or a lineage sample —
a security/compliance defect. See [masking](./masking.md).

## I6 — The per-page pass order is fixed: mask → quality → contract → drift

**Guarantee.** The four protection/validation passes always run in this order.
`contract: on_breach=fail` aborts the page (writes nothing) because breaching
data must never be committed; `schema: on_drift=fail` *defers* its abort until
the page's individually-valid survivors are durable.

**Where.** `run_stream` pass sequence in `crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`.

**If violated.** Reordering could let a quality check pass on unmasked data, or
commit contract-breaching rows. The fixed order removes a footgun config knob.
See [schema](./schema.md), [contracts](./contracts.md), [quality](./quality.md).

## I7 — Every early exit flushes the sinks

**Guarantee.** A source error, a propagated write/flush/state error, a DLQ-budget
abort, a circuit-breaker trip, or a cancellation all funnel through a single
inner future that performs a best-effort final `flush()` before returning.

**Where.** The `loop_result` inner future + trailing flush in `run_stream`.

**If violated.** A buffered sink that only commits on flush (Parquet writes its
footer there; without it the whole file is unreadable; S3 multipart aborts)
would orphan everything written so far. See [pipeline](./pipeline.md).

## I8 — Cancellation is cooperative and flush-completing

**Guarantee.** A `CancellationToken` cancel stops the loop at the **next page
boundary**, flushes the sinks, and returns the *partial* `PipelineResult` as
`Ok`. It never tears down a run mid-`write_batch` from the core's side (a sink
stuck inside a write past the caller's grace is hard-dropped by the caller, not
the core).

**Where.** The `tokio::select! { biased; token.cancelled() … }` page-poll race
in `run_stream`; the executor's `STOP_FLUSH_GRACE` backstop
(`cli/src/executor.rs`).

**If violated.** A cancel that dropped the future immediately would flush
nothing — the difference between a clean stop and a corrupted Parquet file.
See [execution](./execution.md).

## I9 — Config gates are enforced before any run starts

**Guarantee.** An impossible topology — an invalid exactly-once combination, an
unsupported `write_mode × sink`, `schema: evolve` on a schemaless sink,
quarantine without a DLQ — is rejected at config-load in `expand`, so
`faucet validate` fails before a single record moves.

**Where.** `cli/src/expand.rs`; the atomic-watermark gate is re-checked at the
core boundary in `run_stream`.

**If violated.** A config that can't work would fail *mid-stream*, potentially
after partial, unrecoverable side effects.

## I10 — Bookmarks and commit tokens are opaque to everyone but their owner

**Guarantee.** The `StateStore` round-trips a bookmark `Value` without
interpreting it; only the owning source reads it (`apply_start_bookmark`). A
sink stores a commit token as an opaque string and never parses it — the token
may embed a bookmark suffix, which only the pipeline decodes.

**Where.** `StateStore` (`state.rs`), the sink `write_batch_idempotent`
contracts (`traits.rs`), `format_token`/`parse_token` (`idempotency.rs`).

**If violated.** A backend or sink that interpreted the value would couple to
connector internals and break the marketplace's connector-independence. See
[connector SDK](./connector-sdk.md), [extensibility](./extensibility.md).

## I11 — Observability can never fail a run

**Guarantee.** Metrics, spans, lineage emission, and OTLP export are
best-effort. An export error is logged and counted, never propagated; a panic in
an instrumented section is isolated (`catch_unwind`) and surfaced as a `Panic`
error kind, not an aborted process.

**Where.** The decorators in `crates/core/src/observability/`; the lineage
emitter's swallow-and-count path.

**If violated.** A metrics backend outage could take down data movement — an
unacceptable coupling. See [observability](./observability.md),
[standards: logging](../standards/logging.md).

---

## How these compose into delivery guarantees

| Guarantee | Requires | Behaviour on the crash window (I1) |
|-----------|----------|-------------------------------------|
| **At-least-once** (default) | nothing | replays the page — may duplicate |
| **Effectively-once / atomic-watermark** | idempotent sink + deterministic-replay source + durable state + no DLQ | skips or re-anchors the page — no duplication |
| **Effectively-once / keyed-upsert** | upsert-capable sink + `write_mode: upsert\|delete` + `key` | re-upsert is a no-op — no duplication |

## When you change the write path

If your change touches `run_stream`, ask for each invariant above: *does my
change preserve it?* If it relaxes one, that is a design decision requiring an
[ADR](../adr/) or [RFC](../../rfcs/README.md), not a quiet edit. Add a test that
would fail if the invariant regressed.

## Related

- [ADR 0002 — Checkpoint ordering](../adr/0002-checkpoint-ordering.md) · [ADR 0005 — Runtime recovery](../adr/0005-runtime-recovery.md) · [ADR 0007 — Retries](../adr/0007-retries.md)
- [Pipeline engine](./pipeline.md) · [Recovery](./recovery.md) · [State management](./state-management.md) · [Retries](./retries.md)
- [Standards: state & durability](../standards/state.md)
- [Engineering principles](../engineering-principles.md)

# Connector SDK *The `Source` and `Sink` trait contracts and the crate conventions that make every connector interchangeable and every third party a first-class author.* ## Why this exists faucet-stream is a *marketplace*: the value is in the breadth of connectors, and most of them should be writable by people who never touch `faucet-core`. The SDK is the small, stable surface that makes that possible. Two design forces shape it: 1. **Interchangeability** — any `Source` must pair with any `Sink`, so the pipeline is generic and the traits are object-safe (`Box`). 2. **Author ergonomics** — a connector author depends on **one** crate (`faucet-core`), implements a small trait, and gets streaming, checkpointing, observability, retries, and DLQ routing for free. See [ADR 0003 — Builder pattern](../adr/0003-builder-pattern.md) and [extensibility](./extensibility.md). ## The two traits Both live in `crates/core/src/traits.rs` and are `Send + Sync` and object-safe — no associated types, no generic methods, so `Box` / `Box` work everywhere. ### `Source` ```rust #[async_trait] pub trait Source: Send + Sync { // The one required method: async fn fetch_with_context(&self, ctx: &Context) -> Result, FaucetError>; // Everything else is defaulted: fn stream_pages(&self, ctx, batch_size) -> Stream>; // chunks fetch_all fn state_key(&self) -> Option; // None ⇒ not resumable async fn apply_start_bookmark(&self, bookmark: Value) -> Result<(), _>; // resume fn config_schema(&self) -> Value; // schema_for!(MyConfig) fn connector_name(&self) -> &'static str; // friendly metric label async fn check(&self, ctx) -> Result; // faucet doctor probe // capability opt-ins (all defaulted): fn supports_exactly_once(&self) -> bool; fn replay_guarantee(&self) -> ReplayGuarantee; fn is_shardable(&self) -> bool; async fn enumerate_shards(...) ; async fn apply_shard(...); fn supports_discover(&self) -> bool; async fn discover(...) ; async fn capture_resume_position(&self) -> Result, _>; // snapshot→CDC handoff fn dataset_uri(&self) -> String; // lineage } ``` ### `Sink` ```rust #[async_trait] pub trait Sink: Send + Sync { // The one required method: async fn write_batch(&self, records: &[Value]) -> Result; // Defaulted: async fn flush(&self) -> Result<(), _>; // no-op default async fn write_batch_partial(&self, records) -> Result, _>; // DLQ path fn supported_write_modes(&self) -> &'static [WriteMode]; // [Append] default // exactly-once opt-ins: fn supports_idempotent_writes(&self) -> bool; fn dedups_by_key(&self) -> bool; async fn write_batch_idempotent(&self, records, scope, token) -> Result; async fn last_committed_token(&self, scope) -> Result, _>; // schema-drift opt-ins: async fn current_schema(&self) -> Result, _>; // None ⇒ schemaless fn supports_schema_evolution(&self) -> bool; async fn evolve_schema(...) ; // introspection: fn config_schema(&self) -> Value; fn connector_name(&self) -> &'static str; async fn check(&self, ctx) -> Result; } ``` ## The defaulted-method design — capabilities as opt-ins Almost every method above is **defaulted**. This is the mechanism that keeps the SDK both simple *and* backward-compatible: - A minimal connector implements one method (`fetch_with_context` / `write_batch`) and works. - A capable connector *overrides* the defaults for the features it supports — streaming (`stream_pages`), resumability (`state_key` + `apply_start_bookmark`), exactly-once (`supports_idempotent_writes` + `write_batch_idempotent` + `last_committed_token`), upsert (`supported_write_modes`), discovery, sharding, schema evolution. - **Adding a new capability method with a default never breaks an existing connector** — including third-party ones. This is why the SDK can grow without a breaking release. See [stability](../stability.md). ```mermaid flowchart TD Base["implement 1 method
(fetch_with_context / write_batch)"] --> Works["works: at-least-once, bounded via default stream_pages"] Base -->|override stream_pages| Native["native streaming"] Base -->|override state_key + apply_start_bookmark| Resume["resumable / incremental"] Base -->|override supports_idempotent_writes + write_batch_idempotent| EO["exactly-once capable"] Base -->|override supported_write_modes| Upsert["upsert / mirror"] Base -->|override supports_discover + discover| Disc["faucet discover"] ``` ## Crate conventions Every connector crate follows the same layout (see [`.claude/rules/architecture.md`](../../.claude/rules/architecture.md) and the [connector-authoring guide](../contributing/connector-authoring.md)): - **`lib.rs`** — re-exports the config + the `Source`/`Sink` type. First line is `#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg))]` for docs.rs feature badges. - **`config.rs`** — the config struct + sub-enums, deriving `Serialize + Deserialize + JsonSchema`. **No I/O or protocol logic here** — config is pure data, which is what makes `config_schema()` and `faucet init` work. - **`stream.rs` (source) / `sink.rs` (sink)** — the *only* place that performs I/O. Holds reusable clients/pools created in `new()` (never per-call — see [performance](./performance.md)). - Optional helpers — `auth/`, `pagination/`, `extract/`, `convert.rs`, `schema.rs`, `state.rs`. ## What the SDK gives connectors for free Because the pipeline wraps every connector, an author writes zero code for: - **Bounded-memory streaming** — the default `stream_pages` chunks `fetch_all`. - **Checkpointing** — the pipeline persists bookmarks with the correct ordering ([invariants](./invariants.md) I1). - **Observability** — the decorators instrument every source/sink call ([observability](./observability.md)). - **Retries / circuit breaking** — the [resilience](./resilience.md) layer wraps writes; the SDK only asks the sink to honestly report `supports_idempotent_writes()` so retries stay safe ([retries](./retries.md)). - **DLQ routing, quality/contract/masking/drift passes** — all pipeline-level. ## Invariants - **Object safety is non-negotiable.** A new trait method must not require connector-specific types, generics, or associated types, and must have a default so existing connectors keep compiling. - **`faucet-core` is the only required dependency.** If a connector author needs a common crate (async_trait, serde_json, schemars), it is re-exported from `faucet-core`, not added to their `Cargo.toml`. - **`connector_name()` returns a non-empty `&'static str`** — empty falls back to `"unknown"` (and `debug_assert!`s), because it is a metric label. - **Config structs contain no I/O.** Protocol work lives in `stream.rs`/`sink.rs`. ## Trade-offs - **`serde_json::Value` records** maximise author ergonomics (any JSON shape flows) at the cost of allocation and no columnar batching. See [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-json-record-model.md) and [RFC 0002](../../rfcs/0002-arrow-support.md). - **Capabilities as booleans + defaulted methods** is simple and object-safe, but capability discovery is ad-hoc — a candidate for a unified descriptor. See [RFC 0001 — Capability traits](../../rfcs/0001-capability-traits.md). - **One required method** lowers the authoring bar but means a naive connector silently gets only at-least-once, default chunking, and no discovery until it opts in — acceptable, and surfaced by `faucet doctor` / `faucet validate`. ## Failure scenarios - **A connector returns records that don't round-trip as JSON** → surfaces as a typed `FaucetError::Json`/`Source`/`Sink`, never a panic. - **A sink lies about idempotency** (`supports_idempotent_writes() == true` but isn't) → the retry layer will retry writes and may duplicate. This is a connector bug; the honest contract is load-bearing for [invariant I2](./invariants.md). ## Future evolution - A unified capability descriptor ([RFC 0001](../../rfcs/0001-capability-traits.md)). - Shared async-runtime primitives so connectors stop re-implementing bounded concurrency and retry harnesses ([RFC 0005](../../rfcs/0005-async-connector-runtime.md)). - The [Faucet Connector Protocol](../spec/faucet-connector-spec-v0.md) as the formal, versioned contract for out-of-tree connectors. ## Related - [Extensibility](./extensibility.md) · [Overview](./overview.md) · [Pipeline engine](./pipeline.md) - [Stream pages](./stream-pages.md) · [State management](./state-management.md) - [Contributor guide: authoring a connector](../contributing/connector-authoring.md) - [Standards: API design](../standards/api-design.md) - [ADR 0003 — Builder pattern](../adr/0003-builder-pattern.md) · [ADR 0004 — JSON record model](../adr/0004-json-record-model.md) - User guide: [Authoring a connector](../book/src/extending/authoring-connectors.md) · [Connector protocol (FCP v0)](../spec/faucet-connector-spec-v0.md)

1	# Connector SDK
2	
3	*The `Source` and `Sink` trait contracts — small, object-safe, and defaulted, so connectors stay simple and forward-compatible.*
4	
5	## Why it exists
6	
7	faucet-stream is a *marketplace ecosystem*: third parties should be able to publish
8	`faucet-source-*` / `faucet-sink-*` crates against a stable, minimal surface. The
9	two connector traits are the contract that makes that possible. They are designed
10	under three hard constraints — **object-safe**, **minimal required surface**, and
11	**every new method defaulted** — so that `Box<dyn Source>` works, a new connector
12	needs to implement almost nothing, and adding a capability never breaks existing
13	connectors. See [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-builder-pattern.md) and
14	[extensibility](./extensibility.md).
15	
16	## The `Source` contract
17	
18	Defined in `crates/core/src/traits.rs`. The required method is a single fetch; all
19	resumability, streaming, exactly-once, sharding, and discovery are **defaulted**.
20	
21	| Method | Required? | Purpose |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `fetch_with_context` | **yes** | the one primitive: pull records for a context |
24	| `stream_pages` | defaulted (chunks `fetch_all`) | native streaming — override to bound memory |
25	| `state_key` / `apply_start_bookmark` | defaulted (`None` / no-op) | resumability |
26	| `capture_resume_position` | defaulted (`None`) | anchor CDC before a snapshot (replication) |
27	| `supports_exactly_once` / `replay_guarantee` | defaulted (`false`) | delivery capability |
28	| `is_shardable` / `enumerate_shards` / `apply_shard` | defaulted (single shard) | sharded execution |
29	| `supports_discover` / `discover` | defaulted (unsupported) | live catalog introspection |
30	| `config_schema` / `connector_name` / `dataset_uri` | defaulted | introspection & labels |
31	| `check` | defaulted (pulls one page) | `faucet doctor` preflight |
32	
33	A minimal source implements exactly one method and inherits everything else.
34	
35	## The `Sink` contract
36	
37	The required method is a single batch write; everything advanced is defaulted.
38	
39	| Method | Required? | Purpose |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| `write_batch` | **yes** | write a slice of records |
42	| `flush` | defaulted (no-op) | make buffered writes durable |
43	| `write_batch_partial` | defaulted | per-row success/failure for the DLQ path |
44	| `supports_idempotent_writes` / `write_batch_idempotent` / `last_committed_token` | defaulted | exactly-once atomic watermark |
45	| `sink_guarantee` / `dedups_by_key` | defaulted | typed delivery capability |
46	| `supported_write_modes` | defaulted (`[Append]`) | upsert / delete support |
47	| `current_schema` / `supports_schema_evolution` / `evolve_schema` | defaulted | schema-drift handling |
48	| `config_schema` / `connector_name` / `dataset_uri` / `check` | defaulted | introspection & probes |
49	
50	## The capability pattern
51	
52	Advanced behaviour is expressed as **capabilities**: a boolean (or typed) probe
53	method plus the methods that implement it. A sink advertises exactly-once with
54	`supports_idempotent_writes() → true` and then implements `write_batch_idempotent` +
55	`last_committed_token`. The pipeline queries the capability and selects a code path.
56	
57	```mermaid
58	flowchart LR
59	    P[run_stream] --> Q{sink.supports_idempotent_writes?}
60	    Q -->|yes| EO[write_batch_idempotent path]
61	    Q -->|no| DEF[write_batch path]
62	    P --> R{sink.dedups_by_key?}
63	    R -->|yes| KU[keyed-upsert effectively-once]
64	```
65	
66	This keeps the traits object-safe (no associated types, no generic methods) while
67	still letting the runtime specialise. The current pattern uses booleans; a richer,
68	typed capability model is proposed in
69	[RFC 0001](../../rfcs/0001-capability-traits.md).
70	
71	## Connector crate layout
72	
73	Every connector follows the same module layout (enforced by convention, documented
74	in [`.claude/rules/connectors.md`](../../.claude/rules/connectors.md)):
75	
76	- `lib.rs` — re-exports; first line `#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg))]`.
77	- `config.rs` — the config struct + sub-enums, deriving
78	  `Serialize + Deserialize + JsonSchema`. **No I/O here.**
79	- `stream.rs` (source) / `sink.rs` (sink) — the **only** place protocol I/O happens;
80	  holds reusable clients/pools created in `new()`.
81	- optional helpers — `auth/`, `pagination/`, `extract/`, `convert.rs`, `state.rs`.
82	
83	The full authoring walkthrough is in
84	[the contributor guide](../contributing/connector-authoring.md).
85	
86	## Invariants
87	
88	- **Traits are object-safe** — `Box<dyn Source>` / `Box<dyn Sink>` must always work;
89	  no associated types or generic trait methods.
90	- **New trait methods must be defaulted** — adding a capability never breaks an
91	  existing connector. This is a stability guarantee, not a style preference (see
92	  [stability](../stability.md)).
93	- **`faucet-core` is the only required dependency** for a connector author; it
94	  re-exports `async_trait`, `serde_json`, and `schemars`.
95	- **`connector_name()` must return a non-empty `&'static str`** — empty falls back to
96	  `"unknown"` and breaks metric labels.
97	
98	## Trade-offs
99	
100	- **Boolean capabilities** are simple and object-safe but stringly-typed at the CLI
101	  gate (allowlists in `registry.rs`). A typed model would remove the allowlists at
102	  the cost of trait complexity — deferred to [RFC 0001](../../rfcs/0001-capability-traits.md).
103	- **`serde_json::Value` records** maximise author ergonomics at an allocation cost —
104	  see [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-json-record-model.md).
105	
106	## Future evolution
107	
108	- Typed capability traits ([RFC 0001](../../rfcs/0001-capability-traits.md)).
109	- A stable connector ABI for dynamically-loaded plugins
110	  ([RFC 0003](../../rfcs/0003-plugin-system.md)); today plugins link at compile time
111	  via `PluginRegistry` (see [extensibility](./extensibility.md)).
112	
113	## Related

115	- [Extensibility](./extensibility.md) · [Pipeline engine](./pipeline.md) · [Stream pages](./stream-pages.md)
116	- [Connector authoring guide](../contributing/connector-authoring.md) · [Standards: API design](../standards/api-design.md)

1	# Retries
2	
3	*Two retry layers, and the one rule that keeps retries from silently duplicating data.*
4	
5	## Why it exists
6	
7	Transient failures — a 503, a rate limit, a dropped connection, a timeout — are the
8	common case in networked data movement, not the exception. Retrying them turns a
9	flaky dependency into a reliable pipeline. But a naïve retry is one of the most
10	dangerous things a data tool can do: **retrying a write that already succeeded
11	server-side duplicates data**, which is the repository's stated worst bug class
12	(silent downstream corruption). The retry design exists to get the upside without
13	that downside.
14	
15	## The two layers
16	
17	Retries happen in two distinct places, for two distinct reasons:
18	
19	```mermaid
20	flowchart TD
21	    subgraph Source side
22	      REST[rest / xml / graphql] -->|with_retry_policy| RS[execute_with_retry]
23	    end
24	    subgraph Sink side
25	      RS2[run_stream with_retry! macro] --> WB[write_batch* / flush / state_put]
26	    end
27	```
28	
29	1. **Source side** — HTTP sources (`rest`, `xml`, `graphql`) retry their own
30	   requests. The `rest` source predates the unified policy and keeps its own
31	   `max_retries` / `retry_backoff` plus special `429` / `Retry-After` handling;
32	   `xml` / `graphql` use the shared `execute_with_retry` (`crates/core/src/retry.rs`).
33	   A `ResiliencePolicy` is injected via `Source::with_retry_policy`.
34	2. **Sink side** — `run_stream` wraps every `write_batch*`, `flush`, and
35	   `StateStore::put` in a `with_retry!` macro gated on the attached
36	   `ResiliencePolicy`. With no policy the macro is a bare `.await`, so the write path
37	   is byte-for-byte identical to the un-retried path.
38	
39	## The duplication-safety rule
40	
41	This is the single most important line in the retry design (`with_retry_write!` in
42	`crates/core/src/pipeline.rs`):
43	
44	> A non-idempotent `write_batch` is retried **only** when the sink reports
45	> `supports_idempotent_writes()`. Otherwise the write falls through to a bare
46	> `.await` with no retry.
47	
48	The reasoning: a bare `write_batch` makes no atomicity promise. If the request
49	commits on the server but the response is lost, a pipeline-level retry re-sends
50	every row — silent duplication. So faucet-stream *declines to retry* exactly those
51	writes. The idempotent exactly-once path (`write_batch_idempotent`) is always safe
52	to retry, because a replayed token-stamped write is a no-op. See
53	[ADR 0007](../adr/0007-retries.md) and [pipeline](./pipeline.md).
54	
55	## Backoff and jitter
56	
57	Retriable errors back off exponentially with jitter (`crates/core/src/retry.rs`):
58	
59	- **`base * 2^attempt`**, capped at `MAX_BACKOFF` so a large attempt count saturates
60	  rather than sleeping unboundedly.
61	- **Decorrelated `[0.5, 1.5)` jitter** seeded per-call so concurrent retries in one
62	  process draw *different* delays — otherwise they realign and recreate the
63	  thundering herd the jitter exists to break.
64	- **Cancel-aware sleeps** — a cancellation during a backoff sleep returns the last
65	  error promptly so the caller can flush and stop.
66	
67	## What is retriable
68	
69	Only errors classified as transient are retried, gated on
70	`FaucetError::is_retriable` and the policy's `RetryClass` set
71	(`crates/core/src/resilience/classify.rs`): `Http5xx`, `RateLimited`, `Connection`,
72	`Timeout`. A `Config`, `Auth`, or `Json` error is not transient and is never
73	retried — retrying it would only waste time and delay the real failure.
74	
75	## Invariants
76	
77	- **A non-idempotent write is never retried.** (The duplication-safety rule.)
78	- **The no-policy path is unchanged.** Attaching no resilience policy leaves the
79	  write path allocation-free and identical to the pre-resilience code.
80	- **Retries are gated on classification.** Non-transient errors fail fast.
81	- **Jitter is per-call random**, never fixed, to avoid synchronised retry storms.
82	
83	## Trade-offs
84	
85	- **REST keeps its own retry runner** for back-compat; when its `max_retries` /
86	  `retry_backoff` are at defaults the injected policy's `max_attempts` + `base`
87	  apply, but `retry_on` / `max` / `jitter` are inert on REST (honoured in full on
88	  `xml`/`graphql` and every sink-side write). This asymmetry is a deliberate
89	  compatibility concession, documented in [resilience](./resilience.md).
90	- **Declining to retry non-idempotent writes** means a transient sink blip aborts
91	  the run (to be replayed) rather than silently retrying — the safe default, at the
92	  cost of a restart.
93	
94	## Failure scenarios
95	
96	- **Sink commits, response lost, retry fires (idempotent sink)** → the re-sent
97	  token-stamped write is a no-op; no duplication.
98	- **Sink commits, response lost (non-idempotent sink)** → no retry; the run aborts
99	  and the page is replayed on the next run (bounded at-least-once duplication).
100	- **Persistent 5xx** → retries exhaust `max_attempts`, then the circuit breaker may
101	  open — see [resilience](./resilience.md).
102	
103	## Future evolution
104	
105	- Folding the bespoke REST retry runner into the unified policy so `retry_on` /
106	  `jitter` apply uniformly.
107	- Per-sink idempotency hints richer than the current boolean, enabling safe retry of
108	  more write shapes ([RFC 0001](../../rfcs/0001-capability-traits.md)).
109	
110	## Related
111	
112	- [Resilience](./resilience.md) · [Recovery](./recovery.md) · [Pipeline engine](./pipeline.md)
113	- [Design invariants](./invariants.md)
114	- [ADR 0007 — Retries](../adr/0007-retries.md)
115	- User guide: [Resilience cookbook](../book/src/cookbook/resilience.md)
116

# Architecture Decision Records

*The log of major architectural decisions, each with the context and trade-offs that produced it.*

An **Architecture Decision Record** (ADR) captures one significant decision:
what we chose, why, what we rejected, and what we now live with. ADRs are
immutable once accepted — if a decision is later reversed, a *new* ADR
supersedes the old one and links back to it, rather than the old one being
edited. This preserves the reasoning trail for future maintainers who ask "why
is it done this way?".

ADRs describe decisions **already made and implemented**. Forward-looking
proposals live in [`../../rfcs/`](../../rfcs/README.md); an accepted-and-shipped
RFC often produces an ADR here.

## Format

Every ADR follows the same structure: Status · Context · Problem · Decision ·
Alternatives considered · Trade-offs · Consequences · Future work · Related.

## The records

| ADR | Decision | Anchors |
|-----|----------|---------|
| [0001](./0001-stream-pages.md) | Page-based streaming (`StreamPage`) to bound memory at `O(batch_size)` | [stream-pages](../architecture/stream-pages.md) |
| [0002](./0002-checkpoint-ordering.md) | **Write → flush → checkpoint** ordering — the data-integrity keystone | [invariants](../architecture/invariants.md), [recovery](../architecture/recovery.md) |
| [0003](./0003-builder-pattern.md) | Progressive builder APIs over object-safe traits with defaulted methods | [connector-sdk](../architecture/connector-sdk.md) |
| [0004](./0004-json-record-model.md) | `serde_json::Value` as the universal record model | [overview](../architecture/overview.md), [RFC 0002](../../rfcs/0002-arrow-support.md) |
| [0005](./0005-runtime-recovery.md) | Sink-anchored resume — commit tokens embed the resume bookmark | [recovery](../architecture/recovery.md) |
| [0006](./0006-state-management.md) | `StateStore` trait; light backends in core, heavy ones in their own crates | [state-management](../architecture/state-management.md) |
| [0007](./0007-retries.md) | Two-layer retries; never retry a non-idempotent write | [retries](../architecture/retries.md) |
| [0008](./0008-observability.md) | Automatic instrumentation via pipeline decorators | [observability](../architecture/observability.md) |
| [0009](./0009-schema-validation.md) | Fixed-order per-page passes: mask → quality → contract → drift | [schema](../architecture/schema.md) |
| [0010](./0010-pipeline-runtime.md) | Lean core library; all orchestration in the CLI layer | [execution](../architecture/execution.md) |

## Proposing a new ADR

1. Copy the structure of an existing ADR; take the next free number.
2. If the decision is still open, write an [RFC](../../rfcs/README.md) first and
   land the ADR once the decision is made and implemented.
3. Cross-link the architecture pages the decision touches, and add a row above.

## Related

- [Architecture overview](../architecture/README.md)
- [Design invariants](../architecture/invariants.md)
- [RFC process](../../rfcs/README.md)
- [Documentation home](../README.md)
